Grid energy = Required battery energy / Efficiency = 38.4 kWh / 0.90 = 42.67 kWh.

At a sustained charging power of 11 kW, the time to charge is:

Time = Grid energy / Charging power = 42.67 kWh / 11 kW = 3.88 hours, which is approximately 3 hours and 53 minutes.

8. Charge-time estimation
Required inputs
A meaningful estimate requires current SoC, target SoC and the sustained charging power. If current SoC is
missing, ask for it rather than presenting a precise full-charge time.
Energy calculation
Required battery energy equals usable capacity multiplied by the change in SoC. From 20% to 80%, the change
is 60%, so the battery receives 64 kWh x 0.60 = 38.4 kWh.
Efficiency assumption
For a planning estimate on AC, use 90% wall-to-battery efficiency unless measured data is available. Grid
energy for the 20%-to-80% example is 38.4 / 0.90 = 42.67 kWh.
Time calculation
At a sustained 11 kW, 42.67 / 11 = 3.88 hours, approximately 3 hours 53 minutes. Temperature, balancing and
load management can extend actual time.
Do not state a full-charge time when the current state of charge or sustained available power is unknown.

Usable energy
The Orion E4 Long Range has 64 kWh usable battery energy. Gross physical capacity is 68 kWh; charge-time
calculations in this guide use the usable value.
State of charge
The displayed state of charge (SoC) is an estimate of usable energy remaining. A charge-time estimate requires
at least the current SoC, target SoC and available charging power.
Recommended daily range
For routine use, Orion recommends a target between 70% and 80% unless additional range is needed. A 100%
target is appropriate before a longer journey when charging completes close to departure.
